/.excluded: The service saying it runs, for whoever opens its address: no cluster data and no screen reads it.

/health.excluded: The kubelet's probe of this service: no cluster data and no screen reads it.

/ready.excluded: The readiness probe of this service, unready while it is being replaced: no cluster data and no screen reads it.

/metrics.excluded: Prometheus scraping this service's own request counters, not what a screen shows of a cluster.

/api/v1/alertstore/silences/preview.excluded: A step of the silence form, which alerts its matchers would catch. Silences are made on the screen, and a tool does not make them.

/api/v1/api-resources.note: kubectl api-resources, the same list of what the cluster serves.

/api/v1/cluster-config.note: The same cluster details, from kubectl.

/api/v1/cost/status.note: cost answers unavailable without an OpenCost and names the one it read in source.

/api/v1/current.note: The cluster a request is routed to: clusters_list marks it current.

/api/v1/custom-resources/all.note: Instances of every custom resource: the tool lists a kind at a time, and k8s_get_available_api_resources names the kinds.

/api/v1/features.excluded: The switches that decide which tools a caller is offered (features.py GATES): a tool that is off is left out or answers unavailable, which says the same thing.

/api/v1/gateway-policies/all.note: The policy kinds of Gateway API together: the tool lists a kind at a time, and k8s_get_available_api_resources names the kinds.

/api/v1/ingressclasses/{name}/ingresses.note: The Ingresses of one class: the list holds each one's class, and k8s_jq_query picks them.

/api/v1/logsearch/query.note: The screen's LogQL written by hand: the same store and query language as logsearch/logql, which the tool reads.

/api/v1/logsearch/status.note: logsearch answers unavailable when no log store is set for the cluster.

/api/v1/metrics/nodes.note: kubectl top nodes, printed as this route prints it.

/api/v1/metrics/pods.note: kubectl top pods, printed as this route prints it.

/api/v1/metrics/top-resources.note: The dashboard's top consumers: get_pod_metrics and get_node_metrics hold the same usage to sort.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/cronjobs/.note: A CronJob's Jobs: the list holds each Job's owner, and k8s_jq_query picks them.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/daemonset.note: Revisions created in the window, in rollout_history; k8s_get_resources controllerrevisions lists older ones.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/deploymen.note: Revisions created in the window, in rollout_history; k8s_get_resources replicasets lists older ones.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/gateway-p.note: The policy kinds of Gateway API together: the tool lists a kind at a time, and k8s_get_available_api_resources names the kinds.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/logsearch.note: The screen's LogQL written by hand: the same store and query language as logsearch/logql, which the tool reads.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/pods/{nam.excluded: A terminal into a container, an action and not a read: the AI's k8s_execute_command goes through an approval card, and the terminal stays on the screen.
Follows a file for as long as the tab is open. A tool call ends, and logfiles reads the same file with a fixed tail so that nothing keeps running in the container.
Follows a log for as long as the tab is open. A tool call ends, and k8s_get_pod_logs reads the same lines.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/policyrep.note: One object's rows, from the results the tool filters by kind and name.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/services/.note: The Service and its endpoints, through kubectl.

/api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/statefuls.note: Revisions created in the window, in rollout_history; k8s_get_resources controllerrevisions lists older ones.

/api/v1/networktraffic.note: The Resource Graph's lines fold the same flows per workload, and network_drops reads their metrics source.

/api/v1/nodes/{name}/debug-shell/ws.excluded: A root shell on a node, an action and not a read: node shells stay off the AI tools.

/api/v1/nodes/{name}/drain/status.excluded: The progress of a drain someone started on the screen, for that drain's window. What it did shows on the node and its pods, which have tools.

/api/v1/policyreports/resource.note: One cluster-scoped object's rows, from the results the tool filters by kind and name.

/api/v1/policyreports/status.note: policy_reports answers unavailable when the cluster serves no PolicyReport.

/api/v1/prometheus/status.note: prometheus_query answers unavailable when the cluster has no Prometheus.

/api/v1/ws.excluded: The live updates that keep one open list current. A tool reads once, and each list has its tool.

/api/v1/wsMultiplexer.excluded: The live updates that keep open lists current, over one socket. A tool reads once, and each list has its tool.

/api/v1/recordings/{id}/cast.excluded: The recorded terminal output itself, which a person opens on the Session recordings screen, each view its own audited admin.session.read. session_recordings reads that a recording exists and its details, never this.

/internal/clusters/{id}/kubeconfig.excluded: A cluster's credential that tool-server fetches for its own kubectl, service to service. It is never an answer to anyone.

/.excluded: The service saying it runs, for whoever opens its address: no screen reads it.

/health.excluded: The kubelet's probe of this service: no screen reads it.

/metrics.excluded: Prometheus scraping this service's own request counters, not what a screen shows.

/api/v1/auth/oidc/config.excluded: What the sign-in page needs to show its button, before anyone is signed in.

/api/v1/auth/oidc/login.excluded: The browser's redirect to the identity provider: a step of signing in, with nothing to read.

/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback.excluded: The browser's return from the identity provider: a step of signing in, with nothing to read.

/api/v1/auth/jwks.json.excluded: The public keys other services check tokens with, not a screen's data.

/api/v1/auth/.well-known/jwks.json.excluded: The public keys other services check tokens with, at its standard address, not a screen's data.

/api/v1/auth/internal/token-version/{use.excluded: Service to service, so other services can end old tokens. The gateway does not route it.

/api/v1/auth/setup.excluded: Whether a first cluster is registered yet, for the sign-in page's routing, before anyone is signed in.

/api/v1/auth/organizations.excluded: The registration form's dropdown, before anyone is signed in. Tools read clusters, not the sign-up form.

/api/v1/auth/roles.note: Roles and their permissions, for whoever holds admin.review.read: this route is also the registration form's public dropdown.

/api/v1/auth/setup/status.excluded: The first-run setup page's own state, whether a first cluster is registered and how it connected. clusters_list reads the clusters.

/api/v1/auth/setup/rollout-status.excluded: The first-run setup page watching its own rollout after someone submits the form: a step of that action.

/api/v1/auth/me.excluded: The caller's own profile on the Account page, a private screen kept from the AI (utils/aiContext/privateScreens). A tool answer carries who it ran as in access.

/api/v1/auth/permissions.excluded: The list of permission names for the role editor's checkboxes: fixed text for a management form, and access_review reads what each role holds.

/api/v1/auth/admin/audit-logs/export.excluded: The same rows as audit_search as a CSV file for a person to keep. A download is the screen's own audited action.

/api/v1/auth/admin/users.excluded: The user management list: user management stays off the AI tools. access_review reads the accounts for whoever holds admin.review.read.

/api/v1/auth/admin/oidc/groups.excluded: The group names of the user management form's picker: user management stays off the AI tools.

/api/v1/auth/admin/users/{user_id}/clust.excluded: One user's roles in the user management window: user management stays off the AI tools. access_review's cluster_roles reads the same grants.
One user's grants in the user management window: user management stays off the AI tools. access_review's cluster_roles reads the same grants.

/api/v1/auth/admin/clusters/{cluster_id}.excluded: The Clusters screen's access window, where grants are edited (admin.users.update): user management stays off the AI tools. access_review's cluster_roles reads the same grants, for whoever holds admin.review.read, so a role with admin.users.update alone sees it here and not through the AI.

/api/v1/auth/access-requests.excluded: The caller's own requests on the Account page, a private screen kept from the AI (utils/aiContext/privateScreens). access_requests reads everyone's for whoever may decide them.

/api/v1/auth/api-keys/config.excluded: The limits of the Account page's key form, a private screen kept from the AI (utils/aiContext/privateScreens).

/api/v1/auth/api-keys.excluded: The caller's own API keys on the Account page, a private screen kept from the AI (utils/aiContext/privateScreens). access_review's api_keys reads their details for whoever holds admin.review.read.

/api/v1/auth/admin/users/{user_id}/api-k.note: One user's keys, from the same rows the tool searches; a key's value is not in either.

/api/v1/auth/access-review/config.note: settings in the tool's summary holds dormant_days and interval_days.

/api/v1/auth/admin/access-review/export.excluded: The same report as access_review as a CSV file for a person to keep. A download is the screen's own audited action.

/api/v1/auth/dormant-accounts/config.note: settings in the tool's summary holds lock_enabled, lock_days and lock_exempt_admins.

/api/v1/system/deployment-mode.excluded: Whether this install runs on a cluster or on one host, so the Register cluster window can turn off in-cluster mode: a form's setting, nothing about a cluster.

/.excluded: The service saying it runs, for whoever opens its address: no screen reads it.

/health.excluded: The service saying it runs and whether its environment holds a key, for whoever opens its address: no screen reads it and the gateway's /health goes to k8s-service.

/metrics.excluded: Prometheus scraping this service's own request counters, not what a screen shows.

/openapi.json.excluded: The schema FastAPI writes for this service, at its own address. No screen reads it and the gateway does not route it.

/docs.excluded: The API page FastAPI writes for this service, at its own address. No screen reads it and the gateway does not route it.

/docs/oauth2-redirect.excluded: A step of FastAPI's API page, at this service's own address. No screen reads it and the gateway does not route it.

/redoc.excluded: The other API page FastAPI writes for this service, at its own address. No screen reads it and the gateway does not route it.

/api/v1/ai/health.excluded: The kubelet's probe of this service, through its public path: no screen reads it.

/api/v1/ai/config.excluded: The name of the model answering in AI Chat's header and the app's version: the chat's own state, nothing about a cluster. ai_models names the config the chat runs on, for whoever holds admin.ai_models.*.

/api/v1/ai/mcp/config.excluded: How to connect an external agent, in the API keys section of the Account page, a private screen kept from the AI (utils/aiContext/privateScreens): the MCP path and two chart switches.

/api/v1/ai/model-configs/active.note: The config the chat runs on: active names the row whose used_for holds chat, as the cards' Active badge reads it.

/api/v1/ai/suggest-optimization/stream.excluded: The AI explanation on the Optimization screen, a model's answer as it streams, which spends tokens: not a read of data. The optimization tool reads the table it explains.

/api/v1/ai/tool-approvals.excluded: The approval cards waiting in the caller's own conversation, which the chat draws while it runs. An approval is a person's answer to this same chat, and a tool does not give it.

/api/v1/ai/tool-approvals/{approval_id}.excluded: One approval card of the caller's own conversation, which the chat reads to draw it. An approval is a person's answer to this same chat, and a tool does not give it.

/.excluded: The service saying it runs, for whoever opens its address: no screen reads it.

/health.excluded: The kubelet's probe of this service: no screen reads it.

/metrics.excluded: Prometheus scraping this service's own request counters, not what a screen shows.

/api/v1/sessions.excluded: The caller's own conversations in AI Chat's list: the chat itself, nothing about a cluster or about anyone else. A tool would read a person's questions back to the model that answered them.

/api/v1/sessions/{session_id}.excluded: One of the caller's own conversations as AI Chat opens it. The chat gives the model this history itself, so a tool would only read it back.

/api/v1/sessions/{session_id}/messages.excluded: The earlier messages AI Chat loads when the caller scrolls up in their own conversation: the chat's own history, nothing about a cluster or about anyone else.
